skip_reason: Existing-move logistics only — not a sales call. This is an outbound pre-move confirmation call on an already-booked job: Chauny opens with 'I was calling in regards to your move, of course, on the second — do you have a few minutes to kind of go through some details with me?' The move date, both addresses, the home sizes, and the arrival window (1:00-1:30) are already on file and she is reading them back for verification, and the customer already has a rate ('what is included in the rate that you've received'). There is no quote being built, no rate quoted, no estimate presented, no clock explanation, and no booking attempt, because the booking already exists. The inclusions Chauny lists are in answer to a customer question about whether they must self-wrap pictures and mirrors, not a differentiator pitch on a live quote. Grading this against the 9-section sales scorecard would produce a misleadingly low number and pollute the run average.
top_strength: Not graded (skip). Worth noting for the record: Chauny handled the customer's actual anxiety extremely well. Asked whether pictures and mirrors needed wrapping before the crew arrived, she led with 'No, absolutely — that is a standard service for us, so that's no additional charge to you,' then ran the full inclusions list unprompted (gas, taxes, insurance, all wrapping and padding, disassembly and reassembly at the new place, no credit card, transportation, or stair fees) and read the relief back to the customer: 'I just heard a weight just lift off of you.' Her access probing was also better than the file: she established elevator access, confirmed the walk is about twenty feet from building entrance to elevator, got the sectional couch broken down to a piece count (three plus an ottoman, four total), and specifically confirmed every piece fits the elevator so the crew will not need the stairs at all.
coaching_note: Not graded (skip). Two non-scorecard observations for Amanda. First, the highest-leverage miss: the customer twice offered to do prep work ('I still might do a thing or two', 'I might get that done before they come', 'everything else can be kind of consolidated') and Chauny never converted it into the Save Your Ass speech. That customer was volunteering to shorten his own move and the reply he needed was 'Yes, and here's why it pays off — every box you consolidate and every carload you take yourself comes straight off the clock, so prep before move day is the single biggest thing that lowers your bill. Does that make sense?' Prep is in scope on a confirmation call and this was an open door. Second, a data-integrity flag rather than a coaching point: Chauny addressed the customer as 'Matt' at the open and 'ma'am' at the close, the Dialpad speaker label is 'T Thompsonwhite', and the customer twice missed Chauny's name in return ('Seanny, is that right?' then 'Thanks Johnny'). Worth confirming the contact name on that job is right before move day, and worth Chauny slowing down and spelling her name on the greeting.
phone_presence_notes: Real warmth with one standout empathy moment — 'I just heard a weight just lift off of you' after resolving the wrapping worry — plus natural affirmations ('No, absolutely', 'Absolutely, absolutely', 'beautiful') and repeated genuine thanks for each piece of information, and she yielded gracefully when they talked over each other ('oh, no — go right ahead'); held back from a 5 by the name confusion in both directions and by a close that stayed generic rather than referencing anything specific to this customer.
